title: Duplicated symbols due to objects linked twice
description:
See WASM error https://github.com/r-universe/r-lib/actions/runs/25986590671/job/79127792350

The problem exists on all platforms but only emscripten falls over it. I think the problem is that the `$(OBJECTS)` files are also linked in to the libmbedtls lib:

https://github.com/r-lib/webfakes/blob/eb0481d4f0164400d19e3ac81f607430bcf19acc/configure#L21

So we get:

```
emar rcs libmbedtls.a civetweb.o cleancall.o crc32.o errors.o rweb.o .....
...
```

And then again linked in the shared library

```
emcc -s SIDE_MODULE=1 -s WASM_BIGINT -s ASSERTIONS=1 -L/opt/webr/wasm/lib -L/opt/webr/wasm/R-4.6.0/lib/R/lib -s USE_BZIP2=1 -s USE_ZLIB=1 -fwasm-exceptions -s SUPPORT_LONGJMP=wasm -Oz -o webfakes.so civetweb.o cleancall.o crc32.o errors.o rweb.o libmbedtls.a
```

So as a result we get the error that symbols from these objects appear twice:

```
wasm-ld: error: duplicate symbol: mbed_sslctx_init
>>> defined in civetweb.o
>>> defined in libmbedtls.a(civetweb.o)
```

title: Path matching fails if the request has a trailing slash
description:
```r
app <- webfakes::new_app()
app$get("/:name/", function(req, res) res$send("OK"))

server <- webfakes::local_app_process(app)

# This succeeds
httr2::request(server$url("/foo")) |> httr2::req_perform()

# This fails with a "HTTP 404 Not Found."
httr2::request(server$url("/foo/")) |> httr2::req_perform()
```

I'd at least expect the second request to succeed, given that the route definition has the trailing slash. I'm on the fence whether the first one should.

If I use a literal route definition (ie. `app$get("/foo/", ...)`), then I get the opposite result: the request with the trailing slash succeeds but not the one without.

title: Optionally accept `locals`  in handler function
description:
i.e. instead of 

```R
app$use(function(req, res) {
  locals <- req$app$locals
  if (is.null(locals$num)) locals$num <- 0L
  locals$num <- locals$num + 1L
  "next"
})
```

It would be nice to write

```R
app$use(function(req, res, locals) {
  if (is.null(locals$num)) locals$num <- 0L
  locals$num <- locals$num + 1L
  "next"
})
```

title: R CMD check failure
description:
We've been running R CMD check on packages for our package registry manager PRISM ([Home | PRISM](https://prism.dev.a2-ai.cloud/)) and noticed that `webfakes` is failing during tests with 1 snapshot failure. We found the root cause to be `testthat 3.3.2` changing how errors are rendered in snapshots, as the test passes when using `testthat 3.2.3`.

The full error output:
```
checking tests Running testthat.R
Running the tests in tests/testthat.R failed.
Last 13 lines of output:
 new_app_process(app, start = TRUE)
 Condition
 Error:
 - ! failed to start webfakes app process: in callr subprocess.
 + ! ! failed to start webfakes app process: in callr subprocess.
 - Caused by error:
 + Caused by error in `app$listen(port = port, opts = opts)`:
 ! oops
 * Run `testthat::snapshot_accept("app-process", "testthat")` to accept the change.
 * Run `testthat::snapshot_review("app-process", "testthat")` to review the change.
[ FAIL 1 | WARN 0 | SKIP 5 | PASS 403 ]
Error: ! Test failures. Execution halted
```
Investigating the error, we found a snapshot difference in `test-app-process.R`. The error rendering changed in two ways: `!` became `! !`, and `Caused by error:` now includes the originating call.
Here is the failing test:

```
app <- new_app()
app$listen <- function(...) stop("oops")
expect_snapshot(
  error = TRUE,
  new_app_process(app, start = TRUE)
)
```

Expected:
```
Error:
! failed to start webfakes app process: in callr subprocess.
Caused by error:
! oops
```

Actual:
```
Error:
! ! failed to start webfakes app process: in callr subprocess.
Caused by error in `app$listen(port = port, opts = opts)`:
! oops
```
This doesn't appear to be a functional issue, but wanted to flag for visibility. Happy to provide any more details or clarity if needed.

title: decode_url percent‑encoding case differs between curl/libcurl versions (%2f vs %2F)
description:
While comparing test results across environments (for the purpose of updating the Debian package for webfakes), I’ve noticed a behavior difference in the `decode_url` tests that appears to depend on the underlying curl/libcurl stack.

In a newer environment, running the tests via:

```
library(testthat)
library(webfakes)
test_check("webfakes", reporter = "progress")
```

produces the following failure:

```
Failure ('test-decode-url.R:32:3'): decode_url option
Expected: "Return content of foo%2fbar/suffix!"
Actual:   "Return content of foo%2Fbar/suffix!"
```

However, the same test passes unchanged in an older environment.

Failing case:
- webfakes: 1.4.1
- R: 4.6.0 (2026‑04‑24)
-  curl / libcurl: 8.20.0~rc3
- httr: 1.4.8

Passing case:
 - webfakes: 1.4.0
 - R: 4.5.2 (2025‑10‑31)
 - libcurl: 8.19.0
 - httr: 1.4.8

The only difference in the failing assertion is the case of hex digits in a percent‑encoded path segment (%2f vs %2F), which should be semantically equivalent per RFC 3986.

Question:

Is the test intentionally strict about the case of percent‑encoded bytes, or would it make sense to normalize (e.g. lowercase) percent escapes either in the test or in `decode_url()` itself, to avoid backend‑dependent differences?

title: Concurrent requests do not work with HTTP/2
description:
```
web <- webfakes::local_app_process(
  webfakes::httpbin_app(),
  opts = webfakes::server_opts(num_threads = 3)
)

library(testthat)
test_that("", {
  url <- web$url("/delay/1")
  p <- curl::new_pool()
  handles <- replicate(3, curl::new_handle(url = url, http_version = 3))
  resps <- list()
  for (handle in handles) {
    curl::multi_add(
      handle,
      done = function(x) message("one is done"),
      fail = stop,
      pool = p
    )
  }
  st <- system.time(curl::multi_run(timeout = 5, pool = p))
  print(st)
  expect_true(st[["elapsed"]] < 3.0)
})
```

title: Pass URL encoded string as parameter in path
description:
I want to test an endpoint that accepts URL-encoded file paths ("/hello/:file_path"). However, the `app$get()` method throws a 404-error. 

I'm also sharing a real-world example from the [GitLab API](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/api/repository_files.html), where the `file_path` parameter is URL encoded. 

``` r
library(testthat)
library(webfakes)
library(urltools)
library(httr2, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(glue)

app <- webfakes::new_app()
app$get("/hello/:file_path", function(req, res) {
  res$send(paste0("Return content of ", req$params$file_path, "!"))
})
web <- webfakes::local_app_process(app)

test_that("can use hello API", {
  url <- web$url("/hello")
  file_path <- urltools::url_encode("path/to/file.json")

  #This works OK
  # file_path <- "foo"
 
  response <- httr2::request(url) %>%
    httr2::req_url_path_append(file_path) %>%
    httr2::req_perform() %>%
    httr2::resp_body_string()
  
  expected_resp <- glue::glue("Return content of {file_path}!")
  expect_equal(response, expected_resp)
})
#> ── Error: can use hello API ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> <httr2_http_404/httr2_http/httr2_error/rlang_error/error/condition>
#> Error in `httr2::req_perform(.)`: HTTP 404 Not Found.
#> Backtrace:
#>     ▆
#>  1. ├─... %>% httr2::resp_body_string()
#>  2. ├─httr2::resp_body_string(.)
#>  3. │ └─httr2:::check_response(resp)
#>  4. │   └─httr2:::is_response(resp)
#>  5. └─httr2::req_perform(.)
#>  6.   └─httr2:::handle_resp(req, resp, error_call = error_call)
#>  7.     └─httr2:::resp_abort(resp, req, body, call = error_call)
#>  8.       └─rlang::abort(...)
#> Error:
#> ! Test failed
```

<sup>Created on 2025-01-09 with [reprex v2.1.0](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

title: fails when (encoded) spaces are in URL
description:
It appears that `webfakes` does not support urls with encoded (.e.g, `%20`) spaces:

```r
app = webfakes::new_app()
app$get("/testnospace", function(req, res) {
  res$send("url with no space!")
})
app$get("/test%20space", function(req, res) {
  res$send("url with a space!")
})

web <- webfakes::local_app_process(app)

httr::GET(web$url("/testnospace"))$status
#> 200
httr::GET(web$url("/test%20space"))$status
#> 404
```

Is there a way around this, or am I misunderstanding something?

title: #ifdef __MACH__ overmatches and triggers on Hurd.
description:
https://www.gnu.org/software/hurd/hurd/porting/guidelines.html
```
#ifdef __MACH__
Some applications put Apple Darwin-specific code inside #ifdef __MACH__ guards.
Such guard is clearly not enough, since not only Apple uses Mach as a kernel.
This should be replaced by #if defined(__MACH__) && defined(__APPLE__)
```

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

title: teardown env
description:
In the how-to vignette why isn't `testthat::teardown_env()` called right away i.e.

````

```{r eval = FALSE}
httpbin <- local_app_process(httpbin_app(), .local_envir = testthat::teardown_env())
```

If the app process is created in the helper file, then it is ready use after `load_all()`, and (by default) the actual process will be started at the first `$url()` or `$get_port()` call.
You can also start it manually with `$start()`.

Using `.local_envir = testthat::teardown_env())` ensures the process will be stopped after tests are run.

````
